issues.title: [Refactor] diffusion/bcg: Share graph-pool output management
issues.body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #46659 and #46660. The graph-pool allocation and replay copy logic is repeated across attention wrappers and model-specific breaks. These should share output management without forcing different attention implementations through the same compute path.

## Modifications

- Add an optional `output_factory` to `eager_on_graph`: allocate outputs before ending the captured segment, retain weak references, and validate layouts before replay writeback.
- Allow direct writes through `pass_output=True`, preserving H3 embedding's buffer reuse without copying those tensors into themselves.
- Migrate common diffusion attention, H3/VDN attention, H3 embedding, and Qwen Image 2.1 prefix attention. Ordinary eager execution bypasses the factory and extra copies. Existing calls without a factory retain their current behavior.
- Avoid querying the Ulysses group when USP output prediction does not need SP. Update the BCG documentation.

Production code: 115 lines added, 97 removed across five files. Attention algorithms and backend selection are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Validated on one H200 with PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 / CUDA 13.0 at `66de1dcb7a5e7ec9781f66dd751cffbd085182f5`:

- SRT BCG basic/copy/break-helper, diffusion attention outputs, and LTX tests: **35 passed, 33 subtests passed**.
- Qwen Image 2.1 CPU/CUDA, H3 DiT contract, and VDN suites: **181 passed**. Includes exact padded-prefix replay and direct embedding-buffer checks.
- Small real H3 attention modules with random weights: dense SDPA, VDN full-cover, and VDN partial-window branches each captured two segments and matched eager for five changed-input replays at `rtol=0, atol=0`.
- The standalone LTX USP BCG test fails on the base commit without an initialized SP group and passes with this fix.
- Pre-commit and `git diff --check` passed.

Full-checkpoint generation, multi-GPU TP/SP, and AMD/XPU have not been validated in this follow-up.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Bounded Qwen prefix-attention microbenchmark, **not full-model E2E**: one H200, BF16, batch 1, 16 heads x 64, SDPA, 128 padded prefix rows, K/V length Q+384. Measures attention plus one output addition. 20 warmups, then median of 9 batches x 200 calls, synchronized on CUDA. Compared against `c43abd6d9e38a14e81bdb77c648a06353e1c10ee`; execution order was new, base, new repeat.

| Q rows | Mode | Base (us) | New, two runs (us) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 256 | eager | 48.90 | 38.16 / 39.10 |
| 256 | BCG | 82.40 | 80.54 / 81.48 |
| 2048 | eager | 75.45 | 71.83 / 72.00 |
| 2048 | BCG | 97.35 | 96.27 / 96.93 |

Output hashes match across commits. Incremental peak PyTorch allocation is unchanged for BCG and lower for eager in both shapes. BCG performance is effectively neutral; eager avoids an unnecessary allocation/copy. No end-to-end speedup is claimed.

## Checklist

- [x] Run pre-commit.
- [x] Add focused regression tests.
- [x] Update documentation.
- [x] Report correctness and performance evidence with validation limits.
- [x] Follow the existing code style.

issues.title: [Perf] [AMD] diffusion: add a Triton dense attention prefill path for gfx1151
issues.body:
## Motivation

`SDPAImpl.forward` transposes the token-major q/k/v to head-major and hands SDPA a
**non-contiguous** view. On gfx1151 that view costs AOTriton a lot: the same
`attn_fwd` kernel runs at 12.4 / 6.7 / 2.06 TF for 4096 / 8192 / 16384 tokens,
versus 12.4 → 18 TF when the operands are dense. Even the dense number leaves
throughput on the table: a plain Triton prefill kernel reaches 31.8 TF at the
same shape, which is the bulk of diffusion prefill cost.

## What this adds

* `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/attention/flash_attn_dense_triton.py` — a
  non-causal MHA prefill kernel for dense `[B, H, S, D]` operands. It needs no
  masks in the main loop (query length is a multiple of the tile, padding rows of
  K/V are zeroed and their mass is subtracted from the denominator), loads K
  pre-transposed through its strides, and runs `BLOCK_M = BLOCK_N = 64` with 4
  warps and a single pipeline stage. bf16 in, fp32 accumulate, bf16 out; softmax
  keeps the reference's rounding (unscaled q into the WMMA,
  `1/sqrt(D) * log2(e)` on the fp32 scores).
* A gated fast path in `SDPAImpl.forward`: HIP only, `SGLANG_USE_ROCM_TRITON_DENSE_ATTN`
  (default off), bf16, batch 1, equal q/k/v lengths, `head_dim == 128`,
  `seq_len % 64 == 0`, `seq_len >= 4096`, non-causal, no dropout. Everything
  else falls through to the existing SDPA call untouched. Operands are
  materialised head-major once before the kernel sees them; below 4096 tokens
  those copies cost more than the kernel saves, so shorter sequences stay on
  SDPA.

## Numbers (Ryzen AI MAX 395, gfx1151, torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.4, B=1 H=32 D=128 bf16)

Same dense head-major operands for both, kernel-only (median of 10, 3 warmups):

| seq | AOTriton SDPA | Triton | speedup | Triton TF |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4096 | 16.4 ms | 9.7 ms | 1.70x | 28.5 |
| 16384 | 239.3 ms | 138.5 ms | 1.73x | 31.8 |

The 16384 row uses the shipped one-stage pipeline; the 4096 row predates the
stage sweep and is unaffected by it.

What the flag actually changes end to end, i.e. including the layout
materialisation the kernel needs versus the strided call the backend makes today:

| seq | today (SDPA on the view) | with this PR | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4096 | 22.2 ms | 16.6 ms | 1.34x |
| 8192 | 163.6 ms | 54.3 ms | 3.01x |
| 16384 | 2131 ms | 183.3 ms | 11.6x |

The 16K row is the interesting one: AOTriton's strided-operand regression grows
faster than the work does, so at 128 head dim the gap widens with sequence
length. Diffusion DiT self-attention at 2048x2048 sits exactly there.

## Kernel resources and scaling

Compiled at S=16384 the kernel uses 256 VGPR per lane (the RDNA3 limit) with
**zero spills** and 16 KiB of LDS, which keeps four CTAs resident per CU. A
second pipeline stage doubles LDS to 32 KiB, halves residency, and measured
146.3 ms instead of 138.5 ms — that is why the shipped configuration uses one
stage. Of 81 swept `BLOCK_M x BLOCK_N x warps x stages` points, 66 compiled and
this one ranked first; `BLOCK_M = 128` with 2-4 warps spills 350-1149 registers
and drops to 3.8-6.7 TF.

Sweeping the sequence length shows where the materialisation stops paying:

| seq | SDPA on the view | this PR | speedup | kernel vs dense AOTriton |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 1.37 ms | 2.10 ms | 0.65x | 1.81x |
| 2048 | 5.39 ms | 5.58 ms | 0.97x | 1.78x |
| 4096 | 21.7 ms | 16.9 ms | 1.29x | 1.70x |
| 8192 | 150.2 ms | 54.2 ms | 2.77x | 1.62x |
| 16384 | 2180.5 ms | 182.4 ms | 11.95x | 1.64x |
| 32768 | 12932.8 ms | 658.6 ms | 19.64x | 1.65x |

The kernel alone wins at every length (1.62-1.81x against dense AOTriton, and
2.1x to 22x against the strided view); what crosses over is the three
materialisations, which are 69% of the call at 1024 tokens and 20% at 16384.
Hence the 4096-token floor.

Numerics against an fp32 reference: max abs diff 1.1e-3, mean 1.9e-5, no element
above 0.05 (bf16 rounding on both sides).

## Tests

* `test/registered/unit/attention/test_sdpa_triton_dense_attention.py` (CPU, no GPU
  needed; the kernel is mocked): env gate, non-ROCm, torch.compile, causal,
  dropout, fp32, `head_dim != 128`, `seq % 64`, short sequences (`seq < 4096`),
  mismatched lengths, kernel refusal → SDPA fallback; operand strides and `scale`
  forwarded to the kernel. `10 passed`.
* `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_flash_attn_dense_triton.py` (AMD CI):
  fp32-reference numerics at 128/256/512 tokens, zero-padded K/V with `kv_pad`,
  predicate rejections. `4 passed` on gfx1151.

Both were run on gfx1151 with `PYTHONPATH` pointed at a patched copy of the
installed package, so they are not compile-only checks.

## Relation to other work

* #46065 materialises dense SDPA operands; that closes the "strided view" half of
  the gap (AOTriton back to 240 ms at 16K) but not the remaining 1.63x.
* Model-side qkv changes and sparse-attention kernels are out of scope here.

## Caveats

- The default is off: only gfx1151 has been measured. gfx11 should behave the
  same, gfx9x untested — flip the default once there are numbers.
- Sequences below 4096 tokens deliberately stay on SDPA. The floor is the
  measured crossover from the table above, not a derived bound: the kernel alone
  is faster at every length, but the three head-major materialisations dominate
  short calls and make the full path a net loss there.
- End-to-end diffusion (Qwen-Image 2.1 at 2048x2048) throughput is not measured
  in this PR; the benchmark above is operator-level.

issues.title: [Fix] [AMD] diffusion: materialize SDPA operands for long sequences
issues.body:
## Motivation

`SDPAImpl.forward` transposes the `[B, S, H, D]` activations into the `[B, H, S, D]` layout `scaled_dot_product_attention` expects. That transpose is always a strided view, and AOTriton's flash path only applies to **dense** operands, so on HIP a long-sequence attention silently falls back to a generic kernel.

Measured on gfx1151 (AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395, 32 heads x 128, bf16, one SDPA call):

| S | strided | dense | gain |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 1.39 ms | 1.18 ms | 1.18x |
| 2048 | 4.75 ms | 4.35 ms | 1.09x |
| 4096 | 20.84 ms | 15.99 ms | 1.30x |
| 8192 | 184.2 ms | 61.2 ms | 3.01x |
| 16384 | 2255 ms | 242.9 ms | **9.28x** |

The cliff is at S=8192: below it the strided layout still reaches the flash kernel (13-15 TFLOPS), above it drops to 2 TFLOPS while the dense operands hold 18 TFLOPS.

## Modifications

- Extract `sdpa_operands()` from `SDPAImpl.forward`. It still returns the heads-first view, and on HIP it materializes the operands **when `S >= 8192`**.
- The copy is layout-only: values are bit-identical, so there is no accuracy change.
- Below the threshold nothing changes. Qwen-Image 2.1 at 1024^2 (S=4096) is 5.7% *slower* when the copy is unconditional, because the per-layer allocation costs more than the 1.3x kernel gain - so the gate is a sequence threshold, not just a device check.
- The common path (CUDA, and short sequences on any device) keeps the zero-copy view and is the first branch.

## Accuracy Tests

- `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_sdpa_operand_layout.py` (new, runs in the `diffusion-unit-1-gpu-h100` suite): heads-first layout and values; short sequences keep the zero-copy view; long sequences are dense only on HIP; the copy preserves every bit (`torch.equal` against the transposed view).
- End to end, the change only moves tensor layout, so no numerical change is expected by construction. Verified on Qwen-Image 2.1 at 1024^2 and 2048^2 with a fixed seed: identical image, no metric shift.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Qwen-Image 2.1, default environment, `torch_sdpa` backend, gfx1151. Seconds per denoising step (mean over all steps), two runs per arm:

| Shape | before | after | gain |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1024^2 / 20 steps | 3.8524 | 3.8523 | 1.00x |
| 2048^2 / 12 steps | 78.04 / 77.42 | 22.04 / 22.11 | **3.54x** |

Within-arm spread <1%. The 2048^2 gain is AOTriton flash instead of the generic kernel; the 1024^2 row confirms the threshold leaves short sequences untouched.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests.

## Motivation

Qwen-Image 2.1 FP8 inference repeats activation quantization for sibling projections and materializes intermediate BF16 tensors before quantization.

This PR reduces that overhead through shared-input quantization and two fused Triton kernels. Together, these optimizations reduced end-to-end latency by 3.96% on the tested RTX 4090 D workload.

## Modifications
- Share dynamic FP8 input quantization across Q/K/V and gate/up projections while retaining the original separate GEMMs.
- Fuse SiLU + multiplication + dynamic FP8 quantization before the MLP down projection.
- Fuse LayerNorm + modulation + dynamic FP8 quantization before image QKV and gate/up projections.
- Preserve intermediate BF16 rounding and use direct FP32-to-E4M3 conversion to avoid double rounding on SM89.
- Verify the norm and SiLU fusion paths against the existing implementation on first use, falling back on mismatch.
- Extract a shared ATen-compatible Welford reduction for the existing modulation kernel and the new norm/FP8 kernel.
- Share FP8 projection eligibility checks and use explicit forward branches instead of temporary keyword-argument dictionaries.
- Add numerical tests, runtime fallback coverage, and manual microbenchmarks.

The new kernels live under sglang.kernels.ops.activation and sglang.kernels.ops.layernorm.

Runtime dispatch is restricted to supported SM89, TP1, eager dynamic FP8 configurations. The two producer fusions initially target the measured [1, 4096, 4096] image-token shape used for 1024×1024 generation. Unsupported configurations retain the existing path.


## Accuracy Tests

Tested Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo on one RTX 4090 D with 1024×1024 generation, eight steps, seed 42, and a fixed text prompt.

This demonstrates bit-exact output on the tested workload. 

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Configuration: RTX 4090 D, one GPU, Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo, 1024×1024, eight steps, seed 42, TP1 eager execution, FP8 transformer and text encoder, conditioning cache disabled.

### Kernel performance

| Optimization | Before | After | Latency reduction | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Shared-input FP8 quantization | Separate quantization per projection | One quantization per group | Not measured separately | — |
| SiLU + mul + FP8 quantization | 0.569 ms | 0.273 ms | 52.0% | 2.08× |
| LayerNorm + modulation + FP8 quantization | 0.0832 ms | 0.0440 ms | 47.1% | 1.89× |

### Incremental end-to-end performance

Each row measures the benefit of adding that optimization to the preceding implementation.

| Optimization added | Before | After | Latency reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Shared-input FP8 quantization | ~2.734 s | ~2.690 s | ~1.6% |
| SiLU + mul + FP8 quantization | 2.686 s | 2.618 s | 2.54% |
| LayerNorm + modulation + FP8 quantization | 2.866 s | 2.841 s | 0.85% |

### Combined end-to-end performance

Both paths use the same configuration, including unchanged upstream text_encoder=layerwise-offload. The baseline disables all three additions while retaining existing upstream optimizations.

| Metric | All three disabled | All three enabled | Latency reduction | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| End-to-end | 2.957 s | 2.840 s | 3.96% | 1.041× |
| Denoising | 2.472 s | 2.354 s | 4.76% | 1.050× |

Measured using ABBA ordering across four fresh processes, each with one warmup followed by five hot requests. Results are medians over ten measured requests per path.

End-to-end measures the synchronized stage span from input validation through decoding, excluding model loading, warmup, queueing, output serialization, and network overhead.

Peak allocated memory remained 10.840 GiB. Peak reserved memory decreased from 14.178 GiB to 14.139 GiB, a reduction of 40 MiB.

issues.title: [Perf] diffusion: Remove per-step host syncs and uploads in video models
issues.body:
Depends on #46045 (host-sync guards in `test/unit/host_sync_guard.py`); this branch is stacked on it.

## Motivation

Video pipelines run long denoising loops where every blocking host read or pageable upload stalls the host on the previous step's kernels, and several of them rebuilt request-constant RoPE tables or masks on every forward. This PR removes those per-step costs model by model. Outputs are bitwise unchanged.

## Modifications

- **MOVA** (`model_specific_stages/mova.py`, `bridges/mova_dual_tower.py`): the loop uploaded both timesteps every step and `step_from_to` read them back with `float()`, four syncs per step. The paired schedule is uploaded once and the scheduler steps on the host values. Every forward re-uploaded both towers' CPU complex128 RoPE tables (six blocking copies, ~17 MB for audio) and redid the full-sequence concats, and every bridge layer rebuilt its fp32 cos/sin caches (30 layers x 2 directions); tables and bridge caches are built once per request and freed when the loop ends.
- **MiniMax-H3 / FastH3** (`dits/minimax_h3.py`, `minimax_h3_adaln_cache.py`): FastH3 PDD heads copied that step's weight and bias from the host stacks, four blocking copies per step; the stacks are uploaded once per (device, dtype) and indexed by step. The AdaLN online cache indexed its slabs with a 0-dim device slot (a host read, two per step); it now gathers with `index_select` and keeps the old strides.
- **HunyuanVideo** (`dits/hunyuanvideo.py`): the forward built the RoPE cos/sin on the host and copied both to the device every forward (~59 MB per step at 720p x 125 frames). The uploaded tables are kept per request in an underscore `Req.extra` key, which the disaggregation transport skips.
- **Helios** (`helios_denoising.py`, `dits/helios.py`): frame indices were built on the host and uploaded by each of four RoPE embeddings per forward (eight syncs per CFG step); they are built on the latent device. Every block cast the full-sequence [B, L, 6, D] modulation to fp32 (~1.4 GB per block at 384x640); the compact rows are cast once before the expand/concat.
- **Wan family** (`dits/causal_wanvideo.py`, `dits/wanvideo.py`): causal Wan (LongLive2) copied its host RoPE tables to the device every forward; they are uploaded once per request and chunk position. Wan and causal Wan blocks each cast the batch-wide modulation to fp32; the forward casts it once (the per-token TI2V table keeps its fused bf16 path).
- **LTX-2** (`dits/ltx_2.py`, `ltx_2/denoising.py`; paths not touched by #45966): `prepare_video_coords` uploaded two constant tensors per call (every forward on the LTX-2.3 one-stage path, every step for JoyEcho memory coords); they are uploaded once per device. HQ res2s: the SDE coefficient NaN replacement went through a 0-dim boolean index (nonzero on get and set, four calls per step) and is now a `torch.where`; the 100-iteration bongmath refinement hoists its fp64 casts and `h * a21`; the stage-1 step size starts from the step's host sigmas instead of `.cpu()` reads.
- **JoyEcho** (`joy_echo/denoising.py`): every DMD step read sigma and sigma_next with `.item()`; the loop takes fp32 host and device copies of the schedule once. With the memory bank (shot >= 2) the shot-constant cross masks, audio block mask and memory RoPE coords are built once per loop instead of every step.
- **SANA-WM / SANA-Video2** (`sana_wm*.py`, `sana_wm/streaming*.py`, `sana_video2.py`): the cache-type flag was uploaded in every block's clean pass and read back by the next chunk (20 uploads + 20 reads per chunk) and is now a host tensor; self-forcing steps read their timestep once per chunk; `forward_long` windows camera/Plucker inputs once per chunk so the UCPE and Plucker caches hit; the UCPE invalid-ray fix is a `torch.where`; the chunked refiner reads its sigmas from a host copy and builds each block's RoPE once on the device. SANA-Video2 builds its RoPE tables once per latent shape instead of uploading complex128 tables twice per forward.
- **Cosmos3 world models** (`dits/cosmos_dreams.py`, `dits/cosmos3_sim_auto.py`, `cosmos3_simulation/sim_auto.py`): Dreams zeroed null-action V slots by indexing with a Python list in each of 36 layers (a blocking upload each); the slots are per-frame slices. Sim-Auto's scatter/gather indexes, mRoPE frame ids and generated-frame masks are built once per chunk on the device. The default Cosmos3 T2V/I2V loop is untouched (#45967 covers its CFG window).

Tests:
- `test_mova_denoising.py`: steps never upload or read device timesteps (`SyncOnRead` schedule, one upload); RoPE tables built once per request; outputs bitwise equal.
- `test_minimax_h3_pdd_offline.py`, `test_minimax_h3_adaln_cache.py`: heads uploaded once; slab gathers run under `forbid_host_syncs` with the old values and strides.
- `test_hunyuanvideo_rope_upload.py`, `test_wan_step_host_overhead.py`: RoPE tables uploaded once per request (per chunk position for causal Wan), identical tables; blocks receive fp32 modulation.
- `test_helios_step_host_overhead.py`: frame indices live on the latent device; blocks receive fp32 modulation.
- `test_ltx2_step_host_overhead.py`: video-coord constants uploaded once; SDE coefficients under `forbid_host_syncs`; the refinement casts once.
- `test_joy_echo_denoising_host_overhead.py`: host/device sigma copies, steps never read device sigmas, the memory prefix is built once.
- `sana_wm/test_host_overhead.py`, `test_sana_video2.py`, `test_cosmos3_simulation_host_overhead.py`, `test_cosmos_dreams.py`, `test_cosmos3_sim_auto.py`: the SANA-WM, SANA-Video2 and Cosmos3 world-model paths above.

No hunk overlaps #45942, #45943, #45944, #45948, #45965, #45966, #45967, #45977, #45978, #45979 or #45987; each of them still applies on top of this branch.

## Accuracy Tests

2xH200, eager profiles, two requests per model with different inputs. Decoded frames (and audio where the model produces it) are bitwise identical to main:

| model (request) | GPUs | outputs compared | main vs PRs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen-Image-2.1 T2I 1024x1024, 40 steps | 1 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 edit 1024x1024, 40 steps | 1 | pixels | identical (2/2) |

issues.body:
Depends on #46045 (host-sync guards in `test/unit/host_sync_guard.py`); this branch is stacked on it.

## Motivation

Several image pipelines read device values on the host or upload constants with pageable copies inside the denoising loop, or redo request-constant work in every forward. Each such read blocks the host until the stream drains, so it cannot queue the next step while the GPU runs this one. This PR removes them model by model. All values are unchanged.

## Modifications

- **Qwen-Image** (`dits/qwen_image.py`, `pipeline_configs/qwen_image.py`, `qwen_image21.py`, `vaes/base.py`, `qwen_image_layered.py`):
  - Layered built `additional_t_cond` with a pageable `torch.tensor([0])` per CFG branch. The branches got different objects, so the DiT's modulation cache never hit on the negative branch and every step recomputed 60 blocks x 2 modulation GEMMs. Both branches now share one device tensor.
  - Batched prompts of different lengths rebuilt their varlen metadata every forward, uploading the lengths from pageable memory (a sync per step and branch). The metadata is cached by its lengths; each forward gets a fresh dict, since attention may memoize into it.
  - Layered's condition-image encode, the channel-wise VAE stats helper (Qwen-Image edit encode/decode, Krea-2, JoyImage) and Qwen-Image-2.1 decode uploaded latent mean/std per request; they are uploaded once per (device, dtype).
- **FLUX.3 Action** (`flux3_action.py`): `cosmos_unipc` called `float(tick)` on each device tick, a sync per step. The ticks are copied to the host once per request; each step still gets the same device tick.
- **Ideogram-4** (`dits/ideogram.py`, `model_specific_stages/ideogram.py`, `progressive_resolution/ideogram.py`): every forward cast the (B, T+I, 53248) fp32 LLM features to bf16, masked them and ran the RMSNorm and the 53248 -> 4608 projection (plus its TP all-gather) on inputs that never change within a request. The stage projects each branch's conditioning on its first step, inside that step's forward context, and passes it to later steps as `llm_cond`. BCG replays still pass the raw features, which their prompt padder pads; the progressive stage drops the projection when the sequence grows. Decode uploads its latent scale/shift once per (device, dtype).
- **GLM-Image** (`dits/glm_image.py`, `pipeline_configs/glm_image.py`): the eager forward dropped the unconditional branch's prior tokens with `prior_embedding[prior_token_drop] *= 0.0`, two nonzero syncs per forward. It now selects `prior_embedding * 0.0` with `torch.where` (same values, signed zeros included). Decode stats are uploaded once.
- **Krea-2** (`pipeline_configs/krea2.py`): without SP the DiT always got a key mask and ran `bool(mask.all())` every forward. The config decides once per request and passes `mask=None` for unpadded prompts, the maskless path the DiT took before.
- **HunyuanImage-3** (`hunyuan_image3_utils.py`, `hunyuan_image3/ar_stage.py`): per step, a pageable timestep upload, host-built `timestep_embedding` frequencies uploaded on every call (five calls per CFG step), `masked_select` on the request-constant image mask for the scatter and the gather, and per-step condition-timestep uploads on the edit path. Positions, device timesteps and condition timesteps are taken once per request, predictions are gathered by position, and the frequencies are uploaded once per device.
- **SenseNova-U1** (`modeling_neo_chat.py`, `modeling_fm_modules.py`): the CFG-window check compared the device timestep in Python (two syncs per step); the window is computed for the whole schedule with the same fp32 comparisons and read once. The timestep embedder's frequencies are uploaded once per device.
- **SANA** (`dits/sana.py`): every block cast the int64 prompt mask to bool; the forward casts it once.

Tests:
- `test_qwen_image_rope.py`: batched prompts of different lengths build their varlen metadata once, and the second forward matches the first bitwise.
- `test_qwen_image_layered.py`: both CFG branches share `additional_t_cond`; VAE and condition-latent stats are uploaded once.
- `test_qwen_image21.py`, `test_glm_image_dit.py`, `test_ideogram4.py`: decode stats/constants are uploaded once and reused bitwise.
- `test_flux3_action.py`: `cosmos_unipc` with `SyncOnRead` ticks matches the plain run bitwise.
- `test_ideogram4.py`: the LLM projection runs once per branch and every step matches the unprojected forward bitwise; BCG replays get the raw features. `progressive_resolution/test_progressive.py`: a resolution change drops the projection.
- `test_glm_image_dit.py`: the prior-token drop runs under `forbid_host_syncs` and equals the graph path's `masked_fill`.
- `test_krea2_pipeline_config.py`: only ragged prompts carry a key mask.
- `test_hunyuan_image3_denoise_step.py`: timestep frequencies are built once; the image-token scatter/gather runs under `forbid_host_syncs` through the precomputed positions.
- `test_sensenova_u1.py`: timestep frequencies are built once per device.
- `test_sana_dit.py`: the prompt mask is cast once per forward, output unchanged.

The model tests run their tiny DiTs on CUDA when the runner has one (the diffusion unit suite runs on an H100).

No hunk overlaps #45942, #45943, #45944, #45948, #45965, #45966, #45967, #45977, #45978, #45979 or #45987; each of them still applies on top of this branch. #45967 also uploads Qwen-Image-2.1 latent stats once, in the encoding stage; this PR covers decode, a different function.

## Accuracy Tests

2xH200 (1 GPU for Qwen-Image-2.1), eager profiles, two requests per model with different inputs. Decoded pixels are bitwise identical to main:

| model (request) | GPUs | outputs compared | main vs PRs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen-Image-2.1 T2I 1024x1024, 40 steps | 1 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 edit 1024x1024, 40 steps | 1 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Z-Image-Turbo 1024x1024, 9 steps, TP2 | 2 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| FLUX.3 Klein Base 1024x1024, 50 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Ideogram-4 FP8 1024x1024, 20 steps, TP2 | 2 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Cosmos3-Nano T2I 1280x720, 35 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Cosmos3-Nano T2V 1280x720x61, 35 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | frames | identical (2/2) |
| HunyuanVideo 848x480x61, 30 steps, Ulysses 2 | 2 | frames | identical (2/2) |
| LTX-2 two-stage 768x512x121, 40 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | frames + audio | identical (2/2) |
| Wan2.2-T2V-A14B 1280x720x33, 40 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | frames | identical (2/2) |
| MiniMax-H3 T2VA 1344x768 4 s, 12 steps, Ulysses 2 | 2 | frames + audio | identical (2/2) |
| MOVA-360p I2VA 640x352x97, 20 steps, TP2 | 2 | frames + audio | identical (2/2) |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Host syncs inside the denoising stage per step (rank 0, `torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("warn")` around the stage, real server requests):

| model (request) | main: per step in the loop / per request | this PR: per step in the loop / per request |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen-Image-2.1 T2I / edit 1024x1024, 40 steps, 1 GPU | 0 / 1 | 0 / 1 |
| Z-Image-Turbo 1024x1024, 9 steps, TP2 | 0 / 2 | 0 / 2 |
| FLUX.3 Klein Base 1024x1024, 50 steps, CFG parallel | 0 / 1 | 0 / 1 |
| Ideogram-4 FP8 1024x1024, 20 steps, TP2 | 0 / 5 | 0 / 5 |
| Cosmos3-Nano T2I 1280x720, 35 steps, CFG parallel | 1 / 42 | 1 / 42 (the CFG-window read #45967 removes) |

Client latency, interleaved A/B (main, PR, PR, main), fresh server per run, median of 5 measured requests per run:

| cell | round | main | this PR (with #46045) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ideogram-4 FP8 1024x1024, 20 steps, TP2 | 1 | 3.671 s | 3.588 s |
| | 2 | 3.676 s | 3.589 s |
| | median | 3.673 s | 3.588 s (-2.3%) |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 edit 1024x1024, 40 steps, 1 GPU | 1 | 5.288 s | 5.294 s |
| | 2 | 5.312 s | 5.296 s |
| | median | 5.300 s | 5.295 s (-0.1%, noise) |

- Ideogram-4: the denoising stage went from 3.38 s to 3.29 s; the gain is the LLM projection (and its TP all-gather) no longer running in each of the 40 forwards (20 steps x 2 CFG branches). Each run's 5 requests spread under 0.5%.
- Qwen-Image-2.1 had no per-step syncs on main, so only the per-request decode-stats upload goes away; the change is within noise.
- The per-step sync removals for GLM-Image, HunyuanImage-3, Krea-2, SenseNova-U1, Qwen-Image-Layered/batched prompts, FLUX.3 Action and SANA were not benchmarked on GPU here; their unit tests cover them.

issues.title: [Perf] diffusion: Keep every component resident in auto mode when memory allows
issues.body:
## Motivation

`--performance-mode auto` places components from a static per-model allowlist. Above `keep_resident_min_available_gb` (the model's value, else 45 GB for image and 120 GB for video models) only `keep_resident_components` stay resident: the VAE by default, plus the DiT for image models. Everything else streams layer by layer at any memory size:
- Z-Image, Ideogram-4, FLUX, Qwen-Image and LTX-2 stream their text encoder even on a 288 GB GPU. A B300 server log reads `267.1 GiB of free device memory selects layerwise offload for text_encoder` and then `resident=0/36`; Z-Image-Turbo spends 0.066 s of a 0.354 s request moving 3.4 GB over PCIe.
- Wan2.2-T2V/I2V-A14B list `auto` in `dit_layerwise_offload_modes` and set no threshold, so both 14B experts stream layer by layer on every GPU, including H200/B200/B300. That also pins ~54 GB of host memory per rank.

On H100, Z-Image-Turbo with every component resident was 12% faster than auto (0.701/0.699 vs 0.793/0.799 s). The memory-aware fix was meant to come from the warmup-calibrated planner (#37917/#37918), which is not merged. This PR adds a conservative interim rule.

## Modifications

- Memory-rich tier in auto mode (`ServerArgsAutoTuner._fits_all_components_resident`): when the least-free selected GPU has at least twice the per-GPU weight bytes free, every component without an explicit placement stays resident. That means no default layerwise list, no DiT layerwise and component offload cleared, which is the placement `speed` mode gives. Explicit placement flags still win per component.
  - Weights are sized before load from the cached checkpoint's safetensors headers (`checkpoint_component_sizes` in `loader/utils.py`): every `model_index.json` component, counted in its serving precision (`resolve_component_precision`, else as stored), with DiT folders divided by `tp_size`. Text encoders count as full copies even when TP-folded, which is conservative.
  - The tier does not apply, and the per-model policy runs as before, when the checkpoint is not fully cached yet, holds non-safetensors or quantized weights, or is overridden (`--quantization`, `--transformer-weights-path`, SVDQuant, component paths, weights or quantizations, model overlays). It also does not apply with dynamic batching (the factor of two assumes one request's activations), on shared host/device memory (GB10) or on MPS.
  - The rule is platform-agnostic. On ROCm, where auto has no layerwise defaults and offloads the text encoder whole, a GPU that fits the rule now keeps it resident too.
- Wan2.2-T2V/I2V-A14B set `keep_resident_min_available_gb=120` with the DiT and VAE resident. Both experts stay on the GPU on H200-class cards and above; 80 GB cards keep streaming (the two bf16 experts alone are 53 GiB). This holds even when the tier cannot size the checkpoint.

What changes on common GPUs (single GPU unless noted; per-GPU weights at serving precision):

| Model | Weights per GPU | Tier at 2x | H100 80 GB (~79 GiB free) | H200 (~139 GiB free) | 32 GB RTX 5090 (~31 GiB free) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Z-Image-Turbo | 19.1 GiB | 38 GiB | all resident (text encoder was layerwise) | all resident | unchanged |
| FLUX.1-dev | 31.4 GiB | 63 GiB | all resident (T5 was layerwise) | all resident | unchanged |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 | 30.2 GiB | 60 GiB | all resident | all resident | unchanged |
| Qwen-Image | 53.7 GiB (TP2: 34.7) | 107 GiB (TP2: 69) | unchanged (TP2: all resident) | all resident | unchanged |
| Cosmos3-Nano | 32.5 GiB | 65 GiB | all resident | all resident | unchanged |
| Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B | 24.3 GiB (fp32 T5) | 49 GiB | all resident | all resident | unchanged |
| LTX-2 | 65.7 GiB | 131 GiB | unchanged | all resident | unchanged |
| Wan2.2-T2V-A14B | 74.9 GiB (fp32 T5) | 150 GiB | unchanged | both experts and VAE resident (threshold), T5 layerwise | unchanged |
| Ideogram-4 FP8, ModelOpt FP8/NVFP4 | not sized (quantized or `--transformer-path`) | | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged |

B200 (178 GiB free) and B300 (288 GiB) fit every bf16 row, Wan2.2-A14B included. Rows other than Z-Image-Turbo and Wan2.2-A14B follow from the sizing rule; they were not run.

Tests:
- `test_server_args.py`: Z-Image-Turbo keeps every component resident at 139 GiB free and at 45 GiB free (the bf16 serving size fits twice there, the fp32-stored bytes would not). 31 and 23 GiB free resolve exactly as an unsized checkpoint does. Batching, shared host/device memory and an unsized checkpoint keep the text encoder layerwise. Off CUDA, the tier replaces the whole-component text-encoder offload. Wan2.2-A14B keeps both experts and the VAE resident at 139 GiB free while T5 streams, and keeps everything resident at 280 GiB free with sizes.
- `test_weight_utils.py::TestCheckpointComponentSizes`: per-component sizes from a local layout and from a cached hub snapshot without network access; a partially downloaded snapshot (only `model_index.json`, as before the worker downloads), a missing shard, `.bin` weights or FP8 weights stay unsized.
- `conftest.mock_cuda_platform` and the server-args helper stub the sizing, so tests that construct `ServerArgs` for a real repo id never read the runner's HF cache.
- Docs: the `auto` row of the performance-mode table in the deployment cookbook describes the tier.

The new tests fail on main: the sizing helper does not exist there, and the all-resident, serving-precision, off-CUDA and Wan2.2 assertions fail on their own.

## Accuracy Tests

Placement only: the same modules run on the same device, so outputs do not change. On 1xH200, Z-Image-Turbo outputs for five distinct prompts have the same md5s on main and this PR.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Z-Image-Turbo on 1xH200, flagless `sglang serve` (auto mode), 1024x1024, 9 steps. Each run: fresh server, 2 warmup requests, then 5 measured requests, each with a distinct prompt so the conditioning cache never answers the text encoder's work. Rounds interleaved main / PR / main / PR:

| | e2e median (round 1 / round 2) | `TextEncodingStage` | Peak memory per request |
|---|---|---|---|
| main (text encoder layerwise) | 0.952 / 0.954 s | 0.130 s | 15,456 MB |
| this PR (all resident) | 0.867 / 0.863 s | 0.031 s | 22,170 MB |

That is −9% end to end. Every PR sample is below every main sample (0.860–0.872 vs 0.950–1.008 s). The server logs `Auto memory policy for ZImagePipelineConfig: 139.3 GiB free on the least-free selected GPU holds the 19.1 GiB of weights per GPU at least 2x, so every component without an explicit placement stays resident.`

The same PR with all but 30 GiB of the GPU held by another process (the inputs of a 32 GB card) keeps main's placement: text encoder and VAE layerwise, DiT component-offloaded, `TextEncodingStage` 0.130 s.

Earlier evidence for the same gap: H100 Z-Image-Turbo, all resident 0.701/0.699 s vs auto 0.793/0.799 s (−12%).

Wan2.2-T2V-A14B, flagless on 1xH200 (startup only; no timed request): main streams both experts (`transformer` and `transformer_2`: 1.74 GB on the GPU, 26.18 GB pinned on the host each) and the text encoder. This PR loads both experts on the GPU (26.62 GB each) and keeps the VAE resident and the fp32 T5 layerwise, so 52 GB less pinned host memory per rank; the tier itself does not apply (150 GiB needed, 139 free). The end-to-end gain was not measured here.

## CI and baselines

The tier changes placement on the 80 GB H100 lanes wherever the checkpoint is cached and fits twice, so these scenarios will report higher `load_peak_vram_mb` / `runtime_peak_vram_mb` and fail the up-only 1%/2% memory checks by design. Their latency baselines may become stale-high (not a failure). Re-seed them with the usual two-step flow (first run prints the blocks to add to `perf_baselines/h100.json`):
- 1 GPU: `flux_image_t2i`, `zimage_image_t2i`, `zimage_image_t2i_multi_lora`, `cosmos3_nano_t2i`, `cosmos3_nano_t2v` (transformer already pinned resident; the small components join it), `sana_video_2b_t2v`, `longlive2_t2v`, `longlive2_i2v`, `fast_hunyuan_video` (38.5 GiB, 77 of ~79 GiB: closest to the line), `wan2_2_ti2v_5b`, `fastwan2_2_ti2v_5b`, `turbo_wan2_1_t2v_1.3b`, and the Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B family (`wan2_1_t2v_1.3b`, `_teacache_enabled`, `_frame_interp_2x`, `_upscaling_4x`, `_frame_interp_2x_upscaling_4x`, `wan2_1_t2v_1_3b_lora_1gpu`).
- 2 GPUs: `flux_image_t2i_2_gpus`, `zimage_image_t2i_2_gpus`, `zimage_image_t2i_2_gpus_non_square`, `qwen_image21_t2i_tp2`, `wan2_1_t2v_1.3b_cfg_parallel`, `wan2_1_t2v_1_3b_cache_dit_sp_only_2gpu`, `fsdp-inference`.
- `wan2_1_t2v_1.3b_encoder_permanent_residents` exists to test a permanent layerwise resident set on the text encoder, so it now pins the encoder layerwise with `--component-residency text_encoder=layerwise-offload`.
- Unchanged: the 5090 lane (nothing fits twice in ~31 GiB), every quantized or `--transformer-path` case, cases with explicit placement of the components that would move, Wan2.2-A14B, Qwen-Image 1-GPU, LTX and MiniMax-H3 on H100. The B200 lane runs only ModelOpt cases with `--transformer-path`/quantized weights.

The list comes from sizing each case's checkpoint at its serving precision against ~79 GiB free; a runner whose HF cache misses a model keeps main's placement for it.

## Risks

- Steady VRAM grows by the components that used to stream (Z-Image-Turbo +6.7 GB peak, the LTX-2 text encoder on H200, ~53 GiB of Wan2.2-A14B experts on H200). The factor of two leaves at least the weights' size free for activations, assuming one request at a time.
- A checkpoint that is not cached at startup is not sized, so a first start can place components differently from later ones. That is the same placement as main, never more resident.
- `ServerArgs` now reads safetensors headers of a cached checkpoint at startup (local files only, no network).

## Checklist

issues.title: [Perf] diffusion: Serve FA4 head sizes on Blackwell instead of falling back to sm80 SDPA
issues.body:
## Motivation

The CUDA platform decides whether FlashAttention can serve a layer with `FlashAttentionBackend.get_supported_head_sizes()`. That is FA3's list: 32, 64, 96, ..., 256. On Blackwell the FA backend is FA4, which also serves every multiple of 8 up to 128. Other head sizes fall back to `torch_sdpa`. The CUDA platform disables cuDNN SDPA for the whole process, so PyTorch then runs its sm80 FlashAttention-2 kernel (`pytorch_flash::flash_fwd_kernel`).

The Qwen-VL vision towers hit this:
- Qwen3-VL has head size 72. It is the encoder of Qwen-Image-2.1 edit and MiniMax-H3 Ref2VA.
- Qwen2.5-VL has head size 80. It is the encoder of Qwen-Image and Qwen-Image-Edit.

It happens both with the default backend and with `--attention-backend fa`. In both cases the server log shows `Attention backends for text_encoder: torch_sdpa, ...`.

Kernel time on one B300, `[1, H, S, 72]` bf16, non-causal:

| H, S | sm80 FA2 (current) | cuDNN SDPA | FA4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16, 23808 | 9.64 ms | 2.37 ms | 2.35 ms |
| 8, 23808 | 5.09 ms | 1.27 ms | 1.27 ms |
| 16, 4096 | 0.340 ms | 0.082 ms | 0.106 ms |

## Modifications

`CudaPlatformBase._resolve_flash_attention_backend_cls_str`: on Blackwell, a head size that is a multiple of 8 up to 128 now counts as FA-capable, which matches FA4's own check for sm100.
- Default backend: these layers take the Blackwell default, `dynamic_cudnn_sdpa`. That is cuDNN SDPA, with FA4 as the fallback.
- `--attention-backend fa`: they run FA4, including its packed-varlen path.
- Hopper, SM12x and ROCm are unchanged.

Tests: `test_cuda_attention_backend.py` adds two cases on a mocked platform.
- Blackwell: head sizes 72 and 80 resolve to `dynamic_cudnn_sdpa` by default and to FA4 when FA is requested. Head sizes 68 and 136 still fall back to `torch_sdpa`. On main, the 72 and 80 subtests fail.
- Pre-Blackwell: head size 72 keeps `torch_sdpa`.

## Accuracy Tests

All three kernels take bf16 inputs and accumulate in fp32. Against an fp32 reference on random inputs (H=16, S=23808, D=72), their max abs error is 2.8e-4 (sm80 FA2), 2.7e-4 (cuDNN) and 2.5e-4 (FA4).

The table compares the vision tower's outputs on main and on this PR, with the real checkpoints and the same request inputs. Each value is the relative L2 difference.

| | deepstack (block 8) | deepstack (block 16) | deepstack (block 24) | merger output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MiniMax-H3 Ref2VA, 2976x2048 reference, cuDNN | 1.3% | 2.4–2.5% | 3.7–3.8% | 4.7–4.8% |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 edit, `--attention-backend fa` (FA4) | 1.2% | 2.2–2.3% | 3.3–3.6% | 7.1–8.3% |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 edit, default backend (cuDNN) | 1.2% | 2.2–2.3% | 3.4–3.6% | 6.7–7.7% |

The difference grows steadily with depth, which is how bf16 rounding differences add up over 27 blocks. No single layer jumps.

Each kernel against an fp32 reference. The Qwen3-VL vision tower of Qwen-Image-2.1 (27 blocks, head size 72) ran on the benchmark's edit reference (1248x864 after the stage's resize, 4212 patches), once with fp32 weights and math SDPA as the reference, and once in bf16 per attention kernel. Only the attention kernel changes between the bf16 rows. Each value is the relative L2 difference from the fp32 reference, on one B300:

| bf16 attention kernel | deepstack (block 8) | deepstack (block 16) | deepstack (block 24) | merger output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| sm80 FlashAttention-2 (main on Blackwell) | 2.40% | 5.34% | 7.68% | 15.09% |
| cuDNN SDPA (this PR, default backend) | 2.40% | 5.50% | 7.84% | 13.86% |
| FA4 (this PR, `--attention-backend fa`) | 2.40% | 5.21% | 7.55% | 14.91% |
| memory-efficient SDPA (for scale) | 2.39% | 5.27% | 7.64% | 15.24% |

The new kernels are as close to fp32 as main's kernel. FA4 is closer at every depth. cuDNN is within 0.2 points at the deepstack taps and closer at the output. The 7-8% kernel-to-kernel difference in the earlier table is the size of bf16 rounding over 27 blocks, the same order as each kernel's distance from fp32. (The same check on H200 gives FlashAttention-2 / cuDNN / memory-efficient at 14.39% / 15.28% / 15.20% for the merger output.)

End to end on B300 (Qwen-Image-2.1 edit, B300 `--attention-backend fa` command), this PR ran stacked with four other changes; that stack measured 2.626 / 2.637 s against main's 2.751 / 2.771 s. The changes measured on their own account for all but ~60-67 ms of that difference, which is the stored-PNG change plus this one.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Server runs on B300 with each case's serving command. Main and this PR ran side by side on separate GPUs, with requests sent one at a time. The vision-tower time is synchronized wall time around the tower's forward, and the kernel times come from `torch.profiler`.

**MiniMax-H3 Ref2VA**, 2 GPUs with Ulysses 2. The encoder is TP-folded to 8 heads per rank. The reference is 2976x2048, which gives 23808 patches over 27 blocks.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| attention kernels per tower forward | 137.5 ms (27x `pytorch_flash::flash_fwd_kernel`, sm80) | 34.2 ms (27x `cudnn_generated_fort_native_sdpa_sm100_flash_fprop`) |
| vision tower | 182–188 ms | 84.5–84.7 ms |
| text-encoding stage, two warm requests | | 116 ms and 107 ms shorter |
| end to end, 50 steps | 103.41 s | 102.99 s |

**Qwen-Image-2.1 edit**, 1 GPU. The reference becomes 4212 patches over 27 blocks.

| | main | this PR, `--attention-backend fa` | this PR, default backend |
|---|---|---|---|
| attention kernels per tower forward | 9.4 ms | 2.9 ms (FA4) | 2.3 ms (cuDNN) |
| vision tower | 21.0–21.5 ms | 18.0–20.8 ms | 14.5–16.7 ms |

For this case the vision tower is a small share of the encoding stage. Encoding-stage and end-to-end times stayed within run-to-run noise.

The first request at a new image size pays for building a cuDNN plan once per sequence length, about 45 ms. On the H3 case's first request the tower took 128 ms on this PR, against 182 ms on main. FA4 builds no per-shape plan.

issues.title: [Perf] diffusion/qwen-image-2.1: Keep an image prefix's K/V in the packed buffer across steps
issues.body:
## Motivation

Qwen-Image-2.1 computes the prompt prefix (text, and for edits the reference image tokens) once per request and caches its per-layer K/V. Every cached denoising step still rebuilds the attention input from scratch: the packed projection allocates a fresh `[P+S, 3C]` QKV buffer per layer, and the fused Q/K RMSNorm + RoPE + pack kernel copies the cached prefix K/V into its first `P` rows before attention.

For text-to-image the prefix is a few dozen rows and the copy is free. For an edit the reference image makes the prefix about as long as the target (1248x864 reference: 4212 image rows plus text, against 4096 target rows), so the copy doubles the kernel's memory traffic in every layer of every step. On 1xH200 the kernel takes 164 us per call in an edit request against 95 us in a text-to-image request (grid capped at 65535 instead of 32984 blocks): about 88 ms per 40-step request across 32 layers.

## Modifications

`models/dits/qwen_image21.py`, `QwenImage21Attention`:
- After an image-conditioned prefill on the packed path, the request's per-layer cache keeps the packed buffer (`cache["qkv"]`), and its `key`/`value` become views of that buffer's prefix rows, so the separate prefix tensors are freed.
- Cached steps project into the kept buffer (the GEMM writes rows `[P:]` exactly as before) and call the same CUDA kernel with an empty prefix on the target rows, so it normalizes and rotates Q and the target K in place and copies nothing. Attention reads the full buffer.
- Text-only prefixes keep today's compact copy. The kept path needs the packed projection and a verified CUDA pack kernel, single sample, no SP, and no BCG prefix padding; anything else runs as before.

The attention inputs are the same values in the same layout, so outputs are bitwise unchanged. Memory: an edit request holds `[P+S, 3C]` bf16 per layer instead of the `[P, 2C]` prefix plus one transient buffer, about 3.1 GB more at the 1024x1024 edit shape.

Tests (`test_qwen_image21_cuda.py`, CUDA):
- `test_cached_steps_copy_the_prefix_only_for_text`: records every pack-kernel call over a prefill and two cached steps. For an image prefix the cached steps pass an empty prefix and write into the buffer kept by the prefill; for a text prefix they copy the prefix as before.
- `test_cuda_qk_rope_pack_matches_eager_prefill_and_cached_steps`: still bitwise against the eager chain on prefill and cached steps and under BCG replay; its storage check now expects an image prefix to live in the kept buffer and a text prefix to stay compact.

## Accuracy Tests

1xH200, the harness's Qwen-Image-2.1 edit and text-to-image requests: decoded output pixels are bitwise identical to main (md5 of 3 edit and 2 text-to-image outputs, stacked with the other changes listed below).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

1xH200, Qwen-Image-2.1 edit 1024, fresh servers, two GPUs alternated, client medians of 5 (base = main + stored PNG + parallel digest; this column also has the threaded condition resize, see the per-change split below):

| 1 | 5.262 s | 5.176 / 5.174 s |

| | without this PR | with this PR | difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1xH200, 8 rounds | 5.222 s | 5.155 s | −68 ms |
| 1xB300 (`--attention-backend fa`), 6 rounds | 2.657 s | 2.603 s | −50 ms |

issues.title: [Feat] wan-animate-2: Support the distilled model
issues.body: ## Motivation Add native support for [Wan-Animate-2 Distilled](https://huggingface.co/Wan-AI/Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Distilled-Diffusers) (`Wan-AI/Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Distilled-Diffusers`), the distilled variant of the 14B character-animation model of the Wan2.2 family. Like the base checkpoint it takes a **reference image** and a **reference video** and produces a clip of the reference subject performing the reference video's motion; the distilled checkpoint does it in 10 steps at `guidance_scale` 1.0 instead of 40 steps with CFG 3.0. Builds on #42941. The distilled checkpoint is served by the same native `WanAnimate2Pipeline`, selected automatically from the checkpoint directory, as configuration on top of the base support: `log_scale = -1.3` in the attention score modifier, 10 steps at `guidance_scale` 1.0, no CFG parallelism, DPM-Solver++ as the [official](https://github.com/Wan-Video/Wan-Animate-2) command-line implementation samples it. ## Modifications ### New - `Wan_Animate_2_14B_Distilled_Config` (`configs/pipeline_configs/wan.py`): the DiT config with `log_scale` -1.3, the official distillation yaml value (a `log_scale` key in the checkpoint's `transformer/config.json` still wins), and `supports_cfg_parallel=False`. `Wan_Animate_2_14B_Distilled_SamplingParam` (`configs/sample/wan.py`): 10 steps, `guidance_scale` 1.0, everything else inherited from the base sampling params. - `WanAnimate2SchedulerLoader`: the distilled checkpoint is sampled with DPM-Solver++ 2M on the Wan sigma grid, like the base checkpoint, because that is what the model authors' command-line implementation runs for both checkpoints (their distilled yaml's `flow_solver: euler` key is read by no code). The `FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler` named in the distilled repo's `scheduler/scheduler_config.json` is read only by the Diffusers pipeline, which also omits the distilled `log_scale` bias. The loader builds DPM-Solver++ for the distilled config without reading that file and loads the checkpoint's `scheduler/` for the base config; it sets `component_names = []` so it stays pipeline-local, like `WanAnimate2TransformerLoader`; the existing loader-registry test covers both. On the same seed DPM-Solver++ lands 1.8 dB closer to the authors' command-line output than Euler on the shipped grid (33.2 against 31.4 dB, at the same cost): the choice matches the authors' executable implementation; it is not a quality ranking. `--scheduler-class-override` is ignored for the distilled checkpoint and one warning says so (the base checkpoint still honours it). - Registry detectors: both repos share the `model_index.json` `_class_name`; the variant is named only by the `_class_name` of `modular_model_index.json`. The distilled detector matches `WanAnimate2DistilledModularPipeline` or a Wan-Animate-2 path whose directory name carries a `distill` token (a token in a parent directory does not count), the base detector the rest, the distilled one registered first because a directory with `model_index.json` matches both through the shared class. `--model-id Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Distilled-Diffusers` pins the variant explicitly. - Cookbook page `docs/cookbook/diffusion/Wan/Wan-Animate-2.mdx`: variant table, defaults note, distilled presets, request examples, the GB200 distilled benchmark section and troubleshooting entries. The command picker config `docs/src/snippets/configs/Wan/wan-animate-2.jsx` gains a **Checkpoint weights** option in the shape of the Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo one (#43391): per-checkpoint defaults and Request command, CFG parallelism disabled, **Auto** topology resolving to Ulysses and **Auto** text encoder to CPU offload for the distilled checkpoint, the nine measured GB200 layouts as verified recipes, covered by `docs/scripts/tests/wan-animate-2-config.test.mjs`. The model catalog lists both ids. - Unit tests in `test/unit/test_wan_animate_2_config.py` (the two configs, the loader, the CFG-parallel rejection, the `guidance_scale` rejection) and routing in `test_registry.py`; the unit tests run offline on CPU. One GPU CI case, `wan2_2_animate_2_14b_distilled_ref2v` (1 GPU, H100): the base case's inputs at the distilled recipe, at the default video consistency thresholds, with a perf scenario. ### Shared code touched - `registry.py`: the modular-index probe, a pure addition. For a local directory that ships `modular_model_index.json`, the detectors are also probed with that file's `_class_name`; unit test in `test_registry.py`. Nothing else outside the Wan-Animate-2 files changes. ### Supported features - Everything the base pipeline supports in #42941 except CFG parallelism: server warmup, Ulysses, TP and TP x Ulysses, text-encoder CPU offload, DiT layerwise offload (never changes a layout's output, about 2 s in the table below), per-request audio, the bf16 DiT with fp32 encoders and VAE. - Server warmup (`--warmup-mode server`, the `sglang serve` default): three synthetic one-clip startup requests with a built-in reference image and a generated silent reference video: the bounded warmup shape, a residency probe at the largest supported budget, 720x1280, that decides whether the DiT stays resident, and the bounded shape again. A request whose frame geometry differs from the warmup shapes pays a one-time flex-attention autotune on its first occurrence (about 16 s on 1 GPU, 12 to 13 s on 2, 9 s on 4); with `--warmup-mode off` or `request` the first real request pays it instead. - Multi-GPU: at `guidance_scale` 1.0 the CFG-parallel auto-enable rule does not fire, so `--num-gpus N` resolves to Ulysses (`--ulysses-degree N`); `--tp-size N` and `--tp-size 2 --ulysses-degree 2` work as on the base checkpoint. ### Notes on model-specific parameters - The base model's parameters are unchanged (`clip_len`, `fps`, `prompt_ref`, `size` as a pixel-area budget, `video_path` / `video_url`, `seconds` and `num_frames` ignored); the distilled checkpoint changes only the defaults: `num_inference_steps` 10 and `guidance_scale` 1.0. - `guidance_scale` other than 1.0 is rejected at request admission (see **Rejected at startup or request admission**): the distilled checkpoint samples at 1.0 only. - `log_scale` is not a request parameter: it comes from the config class (-1.3) or from the checkpoint's `transformer/config.json` when that file carries the key. ### Rejected at startup or request admission - CFG parallelism for the distilled config, with `Wan_Animate_2_14B_Distilled_Config does not support CFG parallelism`: there is one branch per step, nothing to split. - `guidance_scale` other than 1.0 for the distilled checkpoint, at request admission by the per-request validation hook (`ValueError`, HTTP 400 on `/v1/videos`): `guidance_scale= is not supported by the distilled Wan-Animate-2 checkpoint: it samples at guidance_scale 1.0 only (the distilled recipe has no unconditional branch); omit the field or set it to 1.0.` - Everything the base pipeline rejects in #42941 (`--ring-degree` above 1, `--use-fsdp-inference`, degrees that do not divide the 40 heads, an explicit `--attention-backend`, MXFP8 attention, `enable_teacache` / `enable_spectrum`, `use_img_emb=false`, any `--disagg-role`). ### Deviations from the native-support contract The per-request contract is kept as-is from the base model implementation. The one deviation this PR adds: the distilled checkpoint's scheduler is built in code by `WanAnimate2SchedulerLoader` instead of being read from the checkpoint's `scheduler/`, because the shipped config names a sampler the official reference implementation does not use (see the DPM-Solver++ rationale above). ## Accuracy Tests Inputs of the comparison below, the base PR's inputs, identical for both implementations. | Input 1: reference image (the subject to animate) | Input 2: reference video, 7.9 s at 30 fps (the motion to follow) | | --- | --- | || https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/48c9939c-dd47-4800-a3ee-ed635a03eb3f | **Output, side by side:** sglang distilled (this PR) on the left, the official implementation with the distilled yaml on the right, seed 123. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fc06693e-466e-4b3b-ae69-6e7bfc9ad718 **Output, frame grid at matching timestamps:** sglang distilled top row, official distilled middle row, official distilled with `log_scale` 0 bottom row. Same inputs in both implementations: a 16:9 reference image and a 7.9 s reference video at 30 fps, `size` 640x800 (a 960x528 frame), `clip_len` 37, 10 steps, `guidance_scale` 1.0, identical prompt and negative prompt, default reference-branch prompt; official = the official implementation with the distilled yaml, 236 aligned frames. sglang vs official is 32.8 dB mean PSNR at seed 123 and 31.9 dB at seed 124, while two seeds of either implementation are about 21 dB apart: the two implementations sample the same point, 11 to 12 dB above the two-seed floor, and the floors coincide. | Pair | PSNR mean / min (dB) | SSIM | LPIPS | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | | sglang vs official, seed 123 | 32.8 / 20.7 | 0.945 | 0.035 | | sglang vs official, seed 124 | 31.9 / 20.6 | 0.940 | 0.038 | | sglang seed 124 vs seed 123 (two-seed floor) | 21.0 / 19.1 | 0.780 | 0.126 | | official seed 124 vs seed 123 (two-seed floor) | 20.9 / 18.9 | 0.755 | 0.128 | | sampler A/B, seed 123: DPM-Solver++ on the official grid (this PR) vs official | 33.2 / 20.6 | 0.948 | - | | sampler A/B, seed 123: Euler on the shipped grid vs official | 31.4 / 20.8 | 0.941 | - | - The official code ran on the same GB200 node in bf16 with torch SDPA in place of flash-attn (the flex-attention path that applies `log_scale` was untouched). The band set before measuring for a same-sample match was 22 to 28 dB; the distilled pairs clear it. The same harness on the base checkpoint (40 steps, CFG 3.0) matched sglang's base output at 20.2 dB mean, the two-seed-floor level; that comparison is not part of this PR. - `log_scale` matters: the official output with `log_scale` 0 is 27.2 dB from its `-1.3` output, and sglang's `-1.3` output is closer to the official `-1.3` output (32.8 dB) than to the official `log_scale`-0 output (26.8 dB). - Sampler A/B at seed 123 (the last two table rows; they use a different frame resize, hence 33.2 against 32.8 dB for the same pair). Rows of the grid: DPM-Solver++ on the official grid (this PR), Euler on the shipped grid, official. - Within sglang: DiT layerwise offload and `sglang generate` are byte-identical to the resident 1-GPU server output, and the second request of every server reproduces the first (same md5). Multi-GPU layouts against 1 GPU with the default encoder and VAE parallel settings, PSNR mean / min dB: Ulysses 2 37.4 / 34.7, TP 2 35.9 / 32.4, Ulysses 4 33.3 / 26.4, TP 2 x Ulysses 2 34.8 / 29.7, TP 4 36.8 / 34.5; layerwise offload never changes a layout's output. - Context only: the distilled 10-step output against the base checkpoint's 40-step CFG-3.0 output on the same seed is 16.7 dB, the base model's two-seed-floor level, i.e. a different sample of the same scene. With the benchmark inputs the image gives 1280x704 = 80x44 = 3520 tokens per frame, the video 1264x720 = 79x45 = 3555, and the reference-video copy overflows (`The expanded size of the tensor (3520) must match the existing size (3555)`). A separate PR sizes the in-context attention slot from the larger of the two grids; until it merges, use 640x800 or crop the reference video to the image's aspect ratio.
